source_organization: ICAR - Indian Institute of Horticultural Research (IIHR) / TNAU Agritech
verified_symptoms: Concentric dark brown rings with target-board appearance on older leaves
Yellow halo or chlorotic zone surrounding leaf lesions
Lower leaves affected first, progressing upwards
Collar rot on stems and dark leathery sunken spots at stem end of fruit
distinguishing_features: Concentric rings ('target-board' pattern) distinguish Early Blight from Late Blight (which produces water-soaked irregular lesions with white mould underneath in high humidity).
favorable_conditions: Warm temperatures (24-29°C) with alternating wet and dry periods, frequent rains or heavy dew.
cultural_management: Maintain crop hygiene by removing and destroying infected lower leaves and plant debris.
Avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation to keep foliage dry.
Ensure proper plant spacing for air circulation and practice 2-3 year crop rotation away from solanaceous crops.
Mulch soil around plants to prevent soil-splashing of fungal spores onto lower leaves.
cautious_notes: Chemical fungicide selection should strictly follow state agricultural university (SAU) or local KVK package of practices. Avoid arbitrary spraying.
source_reference: TNAU Agritech Portal - Crop Protection: Vegetables - Tomato - Alternaria Blight; ICAR-IIHR Technical Bulletin No. 42

source_organization: ICAR - Central Potato Research Institute (CPRI) & TNAU Agritech
document_title: Tomato Late Blight Identification and Management
verified_symptoms: Large, irregular water-soaked pale green lesions on leaves turning brown/purplish-black
White downy/cottony fungal growth on underside of leaves under humid conditions
Rapid wilting, browning, and blighting of entire foliage in cool moist weather
Firm, dark greasy or bronze-colored lesions on green tomato fruits
distinguishing_features: Water-soaked lesions with white downy mildew underneath in high humidity, and lack of concentric rings, distinguishes it from Early Blight.
favorable_conditions: Cool temperatures (15-20°C) with relative humidity exceeding 90% or continuous rainfall/fog.
cultural_management: Immediately rogue out severely blighted plants to prevent rapid field-wide dissemination.
Space plants adequately to facilitate rapid drying of leaf canopies.
Avoid excess nitrogenous fertilization which promotes succulent leafy growth vulnerable to blight.
Provide clean drainage in waterlogged field zones.
cautious_notes: Late blight can destroy an entire field within 7-10 days if unchecked. Contact the nearest KVK immediately for localized advisory.
source_reference: ICAR-CPRI Technical Advisory Series; TNAU Agritech Portal Vegetable Crop Protection

source_organization: ICAR - Indian Agricultural Research Institute (IARI) / TNAU
document_title: Bacterial Spot of Tomato and Pepper - Diagnostic Guide
verified_symptoms: Small (2-3 mm) dark brown water-soaked angular spots on leaves, becoming scabby
Spots may coalesce causing leaf yellowing and premature defoliation
Small raised blister-like dark brown scabs on green fruits with white haloes initially
distinguishing_features: Lesions are angular and water-soaked without concentric rings. Unlike fungal blights, bacterial spot thrives in warm rainy weather and does not produce mycelium.
favorable_conditions: Warm temperatures (25-30°C) accompanied by driving rain, wind-driven sand, or overhead irrigation.
cultural_management: Use certified disease-free seeds and seedlings from reputable nurseries.
Avoid handling or weeding wet plants to prevent mechanical bacterial transmission.
Practice drip irrigation rather than overhead sprinkling.
Adopt minimum 2-year rotation with non-solanaceous crops (e.g. cereals, pulses).
cautious_notes: Bacterial infections do not respond to common fungal fungicides. Expert lab confirmation is advisable before treating.
source_reference: TNAU Crop Protection Guide; IARI Plant Pathology Division Disease Fact Sheet 18

source_organization: ICAR - National Research Centre for Integrated Pest Management (NCIPM)
document_title: Management of Tomato Leaf Mold in Protected & Open Field Cultivation
verified_symptoms: Pale green or pale yellow spots on upper leaf surfaces with indistinct margins
Olive-green to velvety brown mold growth on the corresponding lower leaf surface
Leaves curl, wither, and drop prematurely, starting from oldest foliage
distinguishing_features: Prominent olive-green velvety velvety spore masses on the underside of yellow patches, predominantly found in high humidity or greenhouse conditions.
favorable_conditions: High relative humidity (>85%) and moderate temperatures (20-25°C), common in greenhouse or polyhouse setups.
cultural_management: Improve air ventilation and exhaust circulation in polyhouse/greenhouse structures.
Increase plant spacing and prune lower suckers to enhance sunlight penetration.
Avoid late evening irrigation that prolongs nighttime leaf wetness.
cautious_notes: Frequently confused with powdery mildew; verify underside velvet spore mats before chemical intervention.
source_reference: ICAR-NCIPM Integrated Pest Management Package for Tomato; TNAU Agritech Portal

document_title: Septoria Leaf Spot in Solanaceous Crops
verified_symptoms: Numerous small circular spots (2-3 mm) with dark brown margins and sunken grayish-white centers
Tiny black specks (pycnidia) visible inside the gray centers with a hand lens
Severe infection causes lower leaves to turn yellow and drop, exposing fruit to sunscald
distinguishing_features: Distinctive gray center with tiny black specks (fruiting bodies) and dark border; lesions are smaller and more numerous than Early Blight target spots.
favorable_conditions: Warm (20-25°C), wet, and humid conditions; extended leaf wetness.
cultural_management: Remove and burn or compost infected lower leaves as soon as first spots appear.
Stake and cage tomato plants to keep leaves off the ground.
Control solanaceous weeds (such as Solanum nigrum) that act as reservoir hosts.
cautious_notes: Early defoliation directly exposes green tomatoes to severe sunscald. Keep soil adequately mulched.
source_reference: TNAU Agritech Vegetable Pathology; ICAR IIHR Plant Health Advisory

source_organization: ICAR - Indian Agricultural Research Institute (IARI) & TNAU
document_title: Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus (TYLCV) Management Bulletin
verified_symptoms: Upward curling and cupping of leaflet margins
Pronounced yellowing (chlorosis) along leaflet margins and interveinal areas
Severe stunting of young plants and reduced leaf size (bushy appearance)
Flower abortion and failure to set marketable fruit
distinguishing_features: Upward curling with marked interveinal yellowing and severe plant stunting. Vector is the sweetpotato whitefly (Bemisia tabaci); not seed-borne.
favorable_conditions: Hot, dry conditions favorable for whitefly population build-up; high vector density in neighboring fields.
cultural_management: Install yellow sticky traps (15-20 traps per acre) to monitor and mass-trap whitefly vectors.
Use nursery nylon nets (40-mesh) to raise whitefly-free seedlings.
Plant 2-3 border rows of tall barrier crops like maize, sorghum, or pearl millet.
Rogue out and bury virus-infected plants immediately during early vegetative phase.
cautious_notes: Viral diseases cannot be cured once the plant is infected. Management focuses entirely on vector control and nursery hygiene.
source_reference: ICAR-IARI Division of Plant Virology Technical Bulletin; TNAU Agritech Virus Management

source_organization: ICAR - Indian Institute of Horticultural Research (IIHR)
document_title: Tomato Mosaic Virus: Symptoms and Farm Biosecurity
verified_symptoms: Mottling of leaves with alternating light green and dark green mosaic patches
Distorted, blistered, or strap-like leaves ('shoestring' effect)
Internal browning in fruit wall ('brown wall') and uneven ripening
distinguishing_features: Light and dark green mosaic pattern with mechanical transmissibility via contaminated tools, clothes, and hands.
favorable_conditions: High plant handling frequency; spreads mechanically via pruners, stakes, and farm laborers.
cultural_management: Wash hands and dip farm tools in 10% trisodium phosphate (TSP) or skimmed milk solution before handling plants.
Prohibit tobacco smoking/chewing near tomato crops as tobacco products harbor tobamoviruses.
Select certified resistant cultivars (bearing ToMV resistance genes).
cautious_notes: Extremely stable virus that survives in dry soil and dead crop residues for months. No chemical cure exists.
source_reference: ICAR-IIHR Plant Virology Bulletin; TNAU Agritech

source_organization: ICAR - National Bureau of Agricultural Insect Resources (NBAIR) & TNAU
document_title: Tomato Spider Mites Identification and Integrated Management
verified_symptoms: Fine yellow or white stippling (tiny speckles) on upper leaf surface
Fine silken webbing on undersides of leaves and leaf axils
Leaves turn bronze, dry up, and drop under severe infestation
Stunted vine growth and dusty appearance of crop canopy
distinguishing_features: Stippled speckles accompanied by fine silken web threads on leaf underside; mites visible under 10x lens as tiny reddish/yellow-green dots with dark lateral spots.
favorable_conditions: Hot, dry, and dusty weather (temperatures >30°C, low relative humidity).
cultural_management: Spray fine water mist or overhead irrigation periodically to disrupt web structures and reduce dust.
Preserve natural predatory phytoseiid mites by avoiding broad-spectrum synthetic pyrethroids.
Remove heavily infested lower leaves and destroy them away from the field.
cautious_notes: Spider mites are arachnids, not insects or fungi; standard insecticides and fungicides will not control them and may exacerbate outbreaks by killing natural enemies.
source_reference: ICAR-NBAIR Pest Management Guide; TNAU Agritech Entomology Portal

source_organization: ICAR - Directorate of Onion and Garlic Research / IIHR Good Agricultural Practices
document_title: Standard Good Agricultural Practices (GAP) for Tomato Production
verified_symptoms: Vibrant green, uniform foliage without chlorosis, necrotic spotting, or curling
Stout, firm stems with healthy trichomes (hairs) and no vascular browning
Normal flower development and uniform fruit set free of lesions or rot
distinguishing_features: Healthy vigorous foliage displaying typical compound leaf morphology with no signs of fungal lesions, bacterial oozing, or viral distortion.
favorable_conditions: Optimal daytime temperatures (21-27°C) and nighttime temperatures (15-20°C) with well-drained loamy soil rich in organic matter.
cultural_management: Maintain balanced N-P-K fertilization and adequate calcium supply to prevent blossom-end rot.
Adopt regular scouting once weekly to catch pests or foliar spots at early onset.
Practice drip fertigation to conserve water and keep leaf canopies dry.
cautious_notes: Routine preventive maintenance is better than curative chemical applications. Continue weekly field inspection.
source_reference: ICAR Good Agricultural Practices Guide for Vegetable Crops; TNAU Agritech Horticulture

source_organization: ICAR - Central Potato Research Institute (CPRI), Shimla
document_title: Potato Early Blight Diagnosis and Cultural Control
verified_symptoms: Small dark brown necrotic spots on lower leaves with characteristic concentric rings
Spots enlarge up to 1 cm, surrounded by yellow chlorotic halo
Older leaves turn brown and dry up, persisting on stem ('firing' of foliage)
Tubers may develop dark, sunken, circular lesions with raised purple-brown borders
distinguishing_features: Concentric rings ('target spots') on foliage without cottony fungal growth on underside distinguish potato early blight from late blight.
favorable_conditions: Warm weather (24-30°C) with alternating periods of high humidity/rains and dry sunshine.
cultural_management: Plant certified disease-free seed tubers.
Maintain vigorous plant nutrition; potassium and nitrogen stress predisposes foliage to Alternaria.
Avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation and destroy volunteer potato plants and haulms after harvest.
cautious_notes: Ensure proper diagnosis before spraying; early blight symptoms can sometimes be confused with manganese toxicity or senescence.
source_reference: ICAR-CPRI Technical Advisory Series - Potato Pathology; TNAU Agritech

source_organization: ICAR - Central Potato Research Institute (CPRI), Shimla
document_title: Potato Late Blight Forecast and Management Guidelines
verified_symptoms: Water-soaked irregular pale green lesions on leaves rapidly turning purplish black
White downy mildew growth on lower leaf surfaces along lesion margin in wet conditions
Foul odor in severely affected fields due to rapid tissue collapse
Infected tubers show dry rusty-brown discoloration under the skin penetrating into flesh
distinguishing_features: Rapid foliar collapse with white mildew on undersides during cool humid weather. Lacks concentric rings of early blight.
favorable_conditions: Cool temperatures (10-20°C) with relative humidity above 90% and frequent rains/fog (IHMP criteria).
cultural_management: Adopt CPRI Indo-Blightcast forecasting tool to time preventive interventions.
Perform high earthing up (ridging) to create an adequate soil barrier preventing zoospore wash-down into tubers.
Cut haulms (dehaulming) 10-12 days before harvest if late blight appears late in the season.
cautious_notes: Late blight is the most destructive potato disease globally. Consult local KVK or CPRI station immediately upon suspicion.
source_reference: ICAR-CPRI Bulletin No. 51: Potato Late Blight in India; Indo-Blightcast

document_title: Healthy Potato Seed Plot Scheme and Agronomy
verified_symptoms: Lush, upright green foliage without mosaic, leaf rolling, or necrotic lesions
Strong haulm growth with clean subterranean stolon initiation
Healthy white feeder roots free of cysts or galls
distinguishing_features: Uniformly developed compound leaves showing healthy green coloration and normal turgor with zero signs of water-soaking, necrotic rings, or aphid clusters.
favorable_conditions: Cool sunny days and cool nights (15-20°C optimum for tuberization) with sandy loam soil of pH 5.2 - 6.4.
cultural_management: Follow CPRI Seed Plot Technique for aphid-free healthy seed production.
Maintain adequate soil moisture during stolon formation and tuber bulking stages.
Scout for aphid vectors and early blight lesions weekly.
cautious_notes: Maintain good earthing-up to prevent greening of tubers from sunlight exposure.

source_organization: ICAR - Indian Institute of Horticultural Research (IIHR) / TNAU
document_title: Bacterial Spot of Capsicum (Bell Pepper): Identification and Cultural Practices
verified_symptoms: Small yellow-green circular to irregular spots on leaves, becoming dark brown with water-soaked borders
Severe infection causes general chlorosis and heavy defoliation, exposing fruits to sunscald
Raised rough circular warts or scabs on bell pepper fruits
distinguishing_features: Water-soaked brown lesions with dark edges; defoliation from bottom upwards. Note: Bell Pepper is Capsicum annuum (sweet/blocky type); distinct from hot chili varieties.
favorable_conditions: Warm (24-30°C), humid weather with frequent rains or overhead sprinkling.
cultural_management: Use certified disease-free seeds or hot-water seed treatment (50°C for 25 minutes).
Sanitize plant stakes, trellises, and greenhouse benches between seasons.
Ensure proper row spacing and drip irrigation to avoid wet canopies.
cautious_notes: Bacterial spot cannot be controlled by conventional anti-fungal treatments. Do not confuse bell pepper with hot chili.
source_reference: ICAR-IIHR Vegetable Health Advisory; TNAU Agritech Capsicum Protection

document_title: Protected Cultivation of Bell Pepper (Capsicum): Standard Practices
verified_symptoms: Smooth, dark green, glossy leaves with crisp texture and intact margins
Strong branching architecture with vigorous flower buds and clean calyxes
Firm, well-formed four-lobed blocky fruits free of blemishes
distinguishing_features: Uniform dark green foliage without mottling, blistering, or leaf margin burning.
favorable_conditions: Daytime temperatures 25-28°C, nighttime temperatures 18-20°C in well-ventilated naturally ventilated polyhouses or open fields.
cultural_management: Practice two-shoot or four-shoot trellising systems for optimum light interception.
Monitor for thrips and mites under leaf surfaces using blue and yellow sticky traps.
Ensure steady fertigation with calcium and potassium to prevent blossom-end rot.
cautious_notes: Inspect polyhouse screen netting regularly to prevent pest entry.
source_reference: ICAR-IIHR Capsicum Production Manual; TNAU Polyhouse Guide

source_organization: ICAR - Indian Institute of Maize Research (IIMR), Ludhiana
document_title: Maize Rust Diagnosis and Cultural Management Bulletin
verified_symptoms: Small, powdery, oval to elongate cinnamon-brown pustules scattered across both upper and lower leaf surfaces
Pustules rupture epidermal tissue, releasing powdery rusty-red fungal spores on fingers upon touching
As season advances, pustules turn dark brownish-black containing teliospores
distinguishing_features: Pustules appear on BOTH leaf surfaces (unlike Southern Rust which is predominantly on upper surface) and produce cinnamon-brown powdery rub-off spores.
favorable_conditions: Cool to moderate temperatures (16-25°C) with high relative humidity (>95%) and dew.
cultural_management: Sow resistant maize hybrids recommended by ICAR-IIMR for your agro-ecological zone.
Ensure timely early planting to avoid peak rust sporulation periods.
Balance nitrogen fertilizer with adequate potash to improve plant cell wall tolerance.
cautious_notes: Common rust rarely causes severe yield loss in mature corn unless infection occurs before silking on susceptible inbreds.
source_reference: ICAR-IIMR Maize Diseases and Management Manual; TNAU Agritech Maize Pathology

source_organization: ICAR - Indian Institute of Maize Research (IIMR)
document_title: Northern Corn Leaf Blight (Turcicum Leaf Blight) Management
verified_symptoms: Long, elliptical, cigar-shaped grayish-green to tan lesions (2.5 - 15 cm long)
Lesions develop on lower leaves first and spread upward
During damp weather, dark grayish velvety fungal spore masses develop within lesions
distinguishing_features: Cigar-shaped elongated elliptical lesions along veins; differs from Gray Leaf Spot which produces rectangular lesions bounded strictly by leaf veins.
favorable_conditions: Moderate temperatures (18-27°C) accompanied by heavy dews and high humidity.
cultural_management: Deep plowing of crop residues to bury overwintering fungal mycelia.
Practice crop rotation with non-host crops (e.g. soybean, pulses, cotton).
Use certified resistant hybrid varieties.
cautious_notes: Severe blighting prior to silking leads to premature plant death and poor ear fill. Seek local KVK advice.
source_reference: ICAR-IIMR Technical Bulletin: Turcicum Leaf Blight; TNAU Agritech

source_organization: ICAR - National Research Centre for Grapes (NRCG), Pune
document_title: Grape Black Rot Symptoms and Vineyard Canopy Sanitation
verified_symptoms: Small circular reddish-brown leaf spots with dark brown margins and tiny black specks (pycnidia)
Infected berries turn pale, then brown, shriveling into hard, wrinkled black mummies within days
Black sunken cankers on green shoots, petioles, and tendrils
distinguishing_features: Berry mummification where grapes become hard, wrinkled, black shriveled raisin-like mummies persisting on clusters.
favorable_conditions: Warm (20-27°C) and rainy weather with long hours of leaf wetness.
cultural_management: Prune and remove all mummified fruit clusters and infected canes during dormancy.
Manage vineyard trellis canopy to allow maximum sunlight and rapid foliage drying.
Cultivate vineyard soil to bury fallen infected leaf and berry mummies.
cautious_notes: Early season protection from budbreak through fruit set is critical. Consult ICAR-NRCG seasonal advisories.
source_reference: ICAR-NRCG Pune Extension Bulletin: Grape Disease Management; TNAU Agritech

source_organization: ICAR - Central Institute of Temperate Horticulture (CITH), Srinagar / Dr. YSP UHF Nauni
document_title: Apple Scab Management and Orchard Sanitation Guide
verified_symptoms: Olive-green to velvety brown circular spots on leaf undersides and upper surfaces
Spots darken and become thickened, causing leaf distortion and premature leaf fall
Rough, corky, olive-brown to black scabby lesions on fruit surface leading to cracking
distinguishing_features: Velvety olive-green spots turning scabby and corky; fruit skin develops corky cracked scabs.
favorable_conditions: Cool (15-22°C), wet weather during bud break and petal fall periods.
cultural_management: Spray 5% urea on apple foliage just before leaf fall in autumn to accelerate leaf decomposition and destroy pseudothecia.
Prune apple trees to ensure open center and proper air movement through canopy.
Plow orchard floor in early spring to bury overwintered leaves.
cautious_notes: Scab ascospore release is strongly tied to temperature and leaf wetness hours (Mills period). Monitor local state horticulture department warnings.
source_reference: ICAR-CITH Technical Advisory; Himachal Pradesh Horticulture Department Apple Spray Schedule
